expectations: Spawn the real compiled codex-app-server executable in a test-owned CODEX_HOME via codex-uds socket
Use actual remote AppServerSession and typed thread/read + thread/loaded/list to prove first PID is healthy and saved history readable
Terminate first OS PID abruptly; keep an actual TUI App and its unsent draft alive through the disconnect
Spawn replacement PID using same persisted rollout; use TUI's production reconnect() and finish_reconnect() paths
Assert original thread remains selected, offline state clears, historic user message renders, unsubmitted draft is not posted, no synthetic UserTurn operation emitted
Kill test-owned replacement; no live daemon CLI supervisor or updater is touched

native_requirements.source: Only test module + registration + workflow + ledger changed; exact Cargo.lock/deny/version pins and existing high-risk owner holds
native_requirements.cheap: Source integrity, no-review-promotion and Cargo fmt check on Linux before Windows Cargo
native_requirements.windows: windows-2022 hosted runner is allowed only for child-process app-server, which already passed 3F.93; never attempt PID-managed CLI supervisor or job breakaway
native_requirements.build: Build locked production codex-app-server binary and TUI unit test binary once, then one exact selector with timeout and capture all logs
native_requirements.evidence: Fail if any test did not run exactly once and pass; write nonrelease receipt and upload logs

limitations: Real app-server OS process boundary and real TUI reconnect state path, but not the installed/auto-update PID-managed supervisor
Uses a test-owned UnixSocket transport (Windows named pipe) as an explicit remote endpoint to isolate interactive behavior; no proof of the privileged local daemon socket discovery/security handshake
No physical terminal keyboard or PTY rendering; verifies actual TUI app input state and text rendered via Ratatui test backend
Not 21-stage local release acceptance and does not grant 109-path owner approval
No production code, dependency or security policy changes; production stays on 0.4.4
